newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LABOUR PARTY BACKS ENGLAND WORLD CUP BID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LABOUR PARTY BACKS ENGLAND WORLD CUP BID.

text.p: The opposition Labour party, favourites to win a looming election, said on Thursday they would back a bid to stage the World Cup in England in 2006.
Labour leader Tony Blair said: "We will do everything that we possibly can to make sure that the bid for the World Cup in 2006 is successful.

"We are going to put it in our manifesto. We are going to give it every single bit of energy and force we can. I think it's a very sound bid. It's right that it comes to Britain. It will be great for Britain and great for football."

Blair made his commitment as he met Glenn Hoddle, the England coach, Graham Kelly, the chief executive of England's Football Association (F.A.), Keith Wiseman, its chairman and David Davies, director of public affairs.
Blair has already given his personal backing to a cup bid. But the new statement threw the weight of the party behind it.
With Labour rising high in the polls and an election due by May at the latest, Blair is determined to get the message through to the World Cup authorities that England is serious.
Prime Minister John Major has already made clear that the government backs the bid to bring the World Cup back to England, 40 years after it last hosted and won the tournament.

The F.A. decided to launch the bid after the success of Euro 96, which laid to rest fears a tournament in England would be marred by hooliganism and was universally praised for its organisation and excitement.
But it faces strong opposition from Germany.

German officials have accused the F.A. of bad faith, saying there was an implicit agreement that support from Germany for England's Euro 96 bid would be followed by support by the F.A. for Germany's bid to stage the 2006 competition.
But the F.A. has shrugged off the charges.

The rivalry is given added spice by the fact that Germany won the Euro 96 contest after defeating England in the semifinals in a penalty shoot-out, and that England's Wembley victory in 1966 came through a 4-2 final defeat of West Germany.
The F.A. is already preparing its bid and has asked for National Lottery funding to help it.
Media estimates put the cost of staging the tournament at as much as 300 million pounds ($486 million), and just preparing a bid could cost 10 million pounds ($16.2 million) .

But Blair, a passionate football fan who even copied the Euro 96 anthem "Football's coming home" for his last party conference, changing it to "Labour's coming home", said the World Cup would bring money into Britain.
He said the tournament could put as much as 200 million pounds ($323.8 million) in state coffers and inject as much as one billion pounds ($1.6 billion) to the British economy.
